recipes.name: Seven-Layer Taco Dip
ingredients_raw: 1 (6 ounce) can sliced black olives, drained

steps.text: Blend refried beans and taco seasoning in a medium bowl; spread mixture onto a large serving platter.
Mix sour cream and cream cheese in a medium bowl; spread over refried beans.
Top with salsa. Layer tomato, bell pepper, green onions, and lettuce over top.
Sprinkle over Cheddar cheese and garnish with black olives.

raw_recipe.headline: Seven-Layer Taco Dip
raw_recipe.description: This taco dip recipe layers refried beans, salsa, lettuce, veggies, Cheddar cheese, sour cream, and olives to make a delicious party appetizer.

review.reviewBody: I make a recipe very similar to this. I do not use lettuce (as it tends to wilt as it sits out) and I don't use green pepper. Even though I love green pepper, I don't feel it belongs in this recipe (just my opinion). I make homemade guacamole and put that layer on top of the sour cream/cream cheese layer. I found a good guac recipe on this site (LuvAnn's Guacamole) that I use. They always "lick the platter clean" every single time. I've NEVER had leftovers. I serve with Tostitos Scoops as they grab the dip more! Oh and this doesnt' totally spread to fit in a 13x9 pan (mostly the beans don't) so I bought a clear pyrex dish a slightly smaller size. This dish has pretty much become my 7-layer dip dish because it's requested so much at every party! This is an awesome crowd pleaser.

Great recipe, thank you. One word of advice on the container you put it in, an 11 x 7 is no where near large enough. I ended up leaving out the lettuce, not that any one cared! I will use my 9 x 13 next time, I think that will be the perfect size. Thanks again.

Just wonderful!

I actually used a hybrid of user advice here and ended up with this layer combination (from bottom up): Layer 1-refried beans
Layer 2-Cream cheese, sour cream and taco seasoning
Layer 3-Guacamole
Layer 4-Tomatoes, green peppers, green onions, and lettuce
Layer 5-Salsa
Layer 6-Shredded Cheddar cheese
Layer 7-Black beans

I really liked this combination of ingredients and didn't find the lettuce or any of the other vegetables to be bothersome.

I didn't know whether I would prefer this dish hot or cold, so I served it warm the first night, and we had the leftovers cold. I love it either way, and plan to make it again, both for my own family and for get-togethers, for which it is perfect in terms of size.

I drastically reduced the fat and calories by substituting fat-free sour cream, fat-free cream cheese, and reduced fat cheddar. Brought it to a party and NO ONE noticed the change, because all the other flavors made up for it. The dip was scarfed up, and I got requests for the recipe.

I've been wanting to make this for a while, finally had all the right ingredients at the right time. A couple of notes; like others have already suggested, I put some taco seasoning in both the beans and the cream cheese/sour cream blend. I bulked up my chunky salsa with 1/2 cup each of corn, black beans and diced red pepper. Finally, I rearranged the layers--beans, cream cheese/sour cream blend, salsa (veggies of your choice; if not a green pepper fan, maybe green chilis and/or jalapenos would be better here), shredded lettuce, shredded cheese, diced tomato, black olives, green onions on top!
If you put the cutup tomato on the lettuce it won't get lost in the salsa. Looks pretty too.
I put the taco seasoning in with the sour cream & cream cheese. Also instead of green pepper I use a jalapeño or Serrano pepper.

Great recipe ! A lady a church brought 4 of these in 9x13 pyrex pans., to add to our Taco night. ALL of them were gone before the Tacos. I mashed this recipe up with my older recipe. FOR FIRST LAYER, I stiir in 2 to 3 T. salsa into the refried beans, just to make the refried beans more spreadable . FOR THE 2nd LAYER : In a separate bowl, I beat till smooth: 12oz Small curd cottage cheese ( 1-1/2c) 4oz ( 1/2 c) Sour Cream 1 envelope Taco Seasoning, Plus just 1t. more chili powder 1 8oz block cream cheese softened Then, spread that out over refried beans mixture ●■● The Cottage cheese must be 4% fat and SMALL CURD. That changes the texture to very similar to sour cream. Then with the taco seasoning and 1/4 c. sour cream you really do NOT taste cottage cheese. BUT you DO get 3X the amount of protein and far less calories, per serving ,than if you used all sour cream. I do not put lettace on this, but I do serve some on the side . For green peppers, I swap them for pablano peppers ( much milder) OR 1 to 2 (4oz) cans diced green chili peppers OR serve those on the side The rest is the same . With the lower calories and higher amount of protein I serve this for summer dinners & game day meals. It can be made in the morning.. The 1st 2 layers can be made 2 days ahead. So the rest of the layers do not get soggy. I prep those the day before and just assemble on the day I am serving. ( That is what the lady at church did when she made 4 of them). Sometime, I may experiment with a half recipe & use it to stuff halved & seeded jalapeno peppers or pablano peppers, b/c some people like those on the side for scooping instead of chips. OH, in the winter I swap the fresh diced tomatoes for well drained & blotted canned Rotel tomatoes. 1 less thing to chop up

I made it for a potluck and people loved it! I used jalapeno refried beans. I also mixed the taco seasoning with the cream cheese and sour cream which I think brought out the flavor more. I had a bunch of peppers so I added red and orange in addition to the green.
You need to mix the the taco seasoning into the sour cream and cream cheese. It does not get mixed into the refried beans.
I used Bush's Chile's beans (kidneys) and mashed with an immersion blender. That's what I had on hand. Added a little cumin. Drained a bit of juice first. Everyone raves about this recipe!
Made this for Cinco DeMayo for work. I didn't even get a chance to try it. It went that fast.

My family has made a very similar version of this for decades and it is delicious! Tweaks: We don't use the cream cheese and we mix the taco seasoning into 24 oz. of sour cream. Instead of bell pepper we use sliced jalapenos (they go better with Mex, imo). Yum!
It's great everyone loved it, great for hot days you don't feel like cooking!! I put some chopped spring onions and diced tomatos on top with the black olives...
Added a layer of ground beef after refried beans and nacho cheese instead of shredded and got asked for the recipe! Thanks for the idea!

We make this similarly, but we don't care for green pepper, therefore, I chop up a poblano (very mild pepper) instead. I also do not top it with lettuce (I agree-it gets soggy) but rather, have shredded lettuce on the side. We use serving plates, and take a portion, then add the salsa and lettuce

Made this for football playoffs this weekend (01/11/2026). Next time I make this, my partner and I decided we may like to double the refried beans. We had a big container of taco seasoning, and I googled how to measure an ounce. It seemed to say it would be 3 tablespoons. After adding 2 tablespoons to the can of refried beans, it looked like plenty, so I added the third tablespoon to the cream cheese/sour cream mixture. I’m not sure how I may do it with more refried beans. Anyway, I used this one Pyrex that I’m pretty sure is 8x 12. It has a separated thing in the middle. If I use the 9x13 with extra refried beans I think it will be ideal. I also chose to use a bit greener f a lettuce and just made sure it was shredded really small and nice. I used Roma tomatoes. I’d guess I really used just the outside of like 3 Roma tomatoes bc I wanted them to look very red and I quickly realized once putting them into of the salsa that the color didn’t matter haha. They looked good cut up in the dish before I started layering though! I ate mine with Fritos scoops, but my health conscious partner did tortilla chips. Very yummy!! We enjoyed it for the beginning of the 49ers vs Eagles game. I bet this will be a crowd pleaser at Super Bowl parties 🏈.
Didn't add the green pepper and it was great.
I made this for new years day but left off the lettuce and black olives and added some guacamole. Easy good recipe.
